scientific_question: For the exact decimal rational coefficient snapshots of the fifteen frozen rational-model fits, how many distinct real denominator roots lie in each held-out closed interval, and do Z3 and cvc5 independently agree on the corresponding existence or nonexistence obligations?
coefficient_snapshot_rule: Parse each JSON decimal representation directly into fractions.Fraction; the proof concerns this exact rational snapshot, not an exact physical parameter or an exact IEEE-754 binary value

exact_root_rule.arithmetic: Exact rational arithmetic only for root counting and interval isolation
exact_root_rule.squarefree: Remove repeated factors by exact polynomial gcd with the derivative; count distinct real roots
exact_root_rule.sturm: Construct Sturm sequences with exact polynomial division and evaluate sign variations at rational endpoints
exact_root_rule.isolation: Use a Cauchy bound and rational interval subdivision; each returned interval contains exactly one distinct real root
exact_root_rule.closed_interval: Handle exact roots at either endpoint explicitly and retain rational lower and upper bounds

solver_crosscheck_rule.smt_lib: Write exact rational SMT-LIB expressions for every fold, with D(x)=0 and lower<=x<=upper

solver_crosscheck_rule.root_case: When exact Sturm count is positive, expect sat only as a consistency check; the exact Sturm intervals, not approximate solver models, are the root-existence evidence
